attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is an end-anchored `+$` pattern, so on a URL match containing a long run of punctuation followed by a non-punctuation character, the regex engine retries from each start position in the run, giving roughly O(n²) work. The artifact states no maximum description length, so one owner-crafted description could freeze the page for every viewer.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ... const raw = m[0].replace(TRAILING_PUNCT, '');  (no length cap stated)

attacks.claim: Stripping ')' from the end of a URL breaks URLs whose path legitimately ends in a balanced parenthesis, such as Wikipedia article links. The href then points to a different, broken URL.

attacks.claim: `truncated` is set whenever any token exceeds the limit, even when the overflow is only trailing whitespace. The 'Show more' toggle and '…' then appear with nothing meaningful to reveal.
attacks.evidence: if (used + t.value.length <= limit) {...}  ...  return { tokens: out, truncated: true };

attacks.claim: The limit is measured in UTF-16 code units elsewhere, but the out-empty fallback slices by code points. The output can therefore exceed the limit in length, and it can cut between a base character and its combining marks.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });

attacks.claim: Arbitrary external URLs from owner-written text become clickable for every signed-in neighbour, with no interstitial or domain emphasis. This is a phishing exposure, although the raw URL is shown and noopener/noreferrer are set.

attacks.claim: The tests do not cover the 'Show less' path, empty descriptions, multi-line text under white-space: pre-line, or a leading link longer than the limit. Those are the code paths most likely to regress.
